## 固定收益開盤主論述

美國與伊朗再度爆發衝突，推動油價急升；聯準會理事Christopher Waller又明確表示，是否近期再次升息取決於下一份核心通膨數據。美國公債因此於7月13日遭到拋售，2年期殖利率上升7.6個基點至4.285%，來到2025年2月以來的高檔區；5年期上升7.1個基點至4.377%，10年期上升6.3個基點至4.625%，30年期則上升4.5個基點至5.106%。

賣壓集中在較短天期，使殖利率曲線呈空頭趨平。2年與10年期利差收窄1.3個基點至34個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄3.1個基點至82.1個基點。Waller表示，若核心通膨再度偏高，聯邦公開市場委員會便須考慮近期收緊政策；貨幣市場隨後把7月升息的隱含機率，從盤中稍早不到40%提高至約50%。

政策路徑重新定價之際，能源衝擊也再度加劇。美國與伊朗發動新一輪攻擊後，總統Donald Trump宣布恢復封鎖通過荷莫茲海峽的伊朗船隻，並要求使用該水道的其他貨物支付20%的補償金。WTI大漲9.42%至每桶$78.14，布蘭特原油上漲9.59%至$83.30。可觀察到的船舶通行量原已大幅放緩，最新升級局勢進一步削弱航運與石油庫存迅速恢復正常的預期。

實質利率與通膨補償均推動美債殖利率上升。10年期實質殖利率上升3.6個基點至2.336%，10年期損益兩平通膨率增加2.7個基點至2.289%。這顯示投資人不僅反映當前通膨衝擊擴大，也因聯準會的反應函數轉趨緊縮，要求更高的通膨調整後報酬。此次走勢不只是市場擔心能源長期推高物價；短端領跌，是因Waller把廣泛的核心通膨壓力直接連結到聯準會可能在近期會議採取行動。

風險資產強化了盤面的防禦色彩，卻未帶來公債買盤。韓國科技股劇烈下挫並波及美國市場，標普500指數下跌0.79%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.88%，費城半導體指數重挫4.78%。美元指數上漲0.31%；殖利率上升與美元轉強壓過地緣政治避險需求，黃金期貨下跌2.61%至$3,997。VIX上升14.17%至17.16。

不過，當日並未演變成全面性的融資失序。美國財政部3個月與6個月期國庫券標售獲得大量投標，擔保融資市場仍偏寬鬆，聯準會也把每月準備金管理購債規模維持在$100億。兩者的差異相當重要：市場提高了附息公債整條曲線的政策與通膨溢價，但金融體系準備金充裕，現金投資人仍持續承接短期政府債券。

## 油價與Waller把緊縮風險推向7月

荷莫茲海峽周邊情勢再度惡化，是當日最直接的催化因素。一艘貨櫃輪遇襲後，美軍進一步發動攻擊，伊朗則報復美國在區域內的盟友與基地。華府與德黑蘭對海峽是否開放各執一詞，但可觀察到的通行活動已幾乎停止，週日的船舶通行總量降至一個月最低。

Trump隨後表示，美國將恢復封鎖伊朗船隻，並要求所有其他通過荷莫茲海峽的貨物支付20%的補償金。德黑蘭接受由提供安全通行者取得補償的原則，但認為擬議費率過高。白宮並未說明如何收取這筆費用，也未交代波斯灣盟友是否同意。

若付諸實施，這項收費對商業運輸的影響將相當顯著。按當前油價計算，一艘滿載的超大型油輪若支付20%，金額約為$3,200萬；相較之下，先前所述的伊朗通行費最高約為$200萬。美國中央司令部表示，恢復封鎖將於7月14日美東時間16:00開始，因此這是已宣布、但尚未納入週一實際航運制度的未來條件。即使如此，消息本身已降低船運迅速恢復正常的可能性，因而影響週一市場評估。

油價反應也相當劇烈。布蘭特原油盤中突破$80，紐約收盤時漲幅超過9%；WTI則創下逾三個月來最大單日漲幅。兩項指標即使大漲後仍低於戰事早期高點，但走勢已逆轉7月10日美債交易時伴隨的短暫能源壓力緩解。債市因此必須同時反映供應風險再起，以及燃料價格進一步上漲、強化原已偏高之基礎通膨的可能性。

Waller明確指出了第二條傳導管道。他表示，若本週數據再次顯示核心通膨偏高，決策官員便須考慮近期收緊政策。他認為經濟狀況良好，勞動市場穩定、消費需求具有韌性；但關稅、能源價格與人工智慧基礎設施支出都在增加物價壓力，使政策走到十字路口。

他的疑慮不僅來自原油再度上漲。截至5月止的一年，核心個人消費支出通膨率已達3.4%，而且自1月起持續上升，早於最近一輪美伊戰事。Waller認為，基礎通膨上升已呈現足夠的持續性，必須關注其擴散廣度，不能只視為暫時性的能源擾動。

這項判斷的條件也同樣重要。Waller表示，需要連續數月較低的核心數據，才能確認通膨正朝正確方向發展，但他仍認為這種結果可能出現；若確實如此，他會支持維持利率不變。他也指出，勞動市場並未呈現2021至2022年通膨期間的過度緊俏，通膨預期也仍受到錨定。

因此，Waller的立場仍有條件，並非無條件主張立即升息。較溫和的核心數據將支持按兵不動；若結果再次強勁，近期緊縮的理由便會增強。聯準會6月會議一致決議維持目標利率不變，但會議紀錄顯示，少數官員認為有理由升息。提交預測的18名決策官員中，有一半預期2026年至少升息1碼，主席Kevin Warsh則未提交利率預測。

美債定價在最直接受這項條件影響的區段反應最強。2年期殖利率升幅略高於5年期與10年期，並明顯高於30年期。儘管過去一個月四個指標天期的殖利率全數上升，2年與30年期利差仍已收窄6.5個基點。投資人同時提高對通膨與緊縮政策的補償要求，但最新一輪調整主要集中在未來幾次FOMC決策的路徑。

10年期殖利率的拆解顯示，單一因素不足以解釋這波賣壓。損益兩平通膨率上升2.7個基點，反映油價大漲後通膨溢價再起；實質殖利率上升3.6個基點，則納入聯準會可能回應的預期，以及經濟活動仍具韌性、公私部門大量借款帶來的持續負擔。名目10年期殖利率升至5月以來最高。

交易活動也隨行情擴大。美國公債現貨市場以面額計算的交易量達$9,242億，較前一交易日增加15%；名目附息債交易量增加16.4%至$7,218億。超過7年、但不超過10年期券種的成交量增加32.2%至$1,265億。這些數字衡量的是雙向交易，而非投資人的買賣方向，但顯示這波拋售發生在交投更活躍的交易日，尤其集中於指標券區段。

跨資產反應也不只反映能源衝擊。韓國科技股在經歷一年異常強勁的漲勢後再度劇烈反轉。MSCI韓國指數截至6月止的12個月漲幅超過250%，但週一下跌後已較6月高點低28%。SK海力士在首爾創紀錄重挫15%，其美國存託憑證也下跌9.3%，顯示市場對人工智慧部位過度擁擠的疑慮已蔓延至美國交易。

台積電的營運數據卻呈現鮮明對比：季度營收成長36%至新台幣1.27兆元，其中6月營收年增68%。這項分歧不代表人工智慧需求已經崩跌，而是顯示強勁的營運成果可以與異常脆弱的部位和估值並存。對利率市場而言，這一點相當重要：即使相關股票的波動加劇，AI建設仍同時帶來實質需求與極為龐大的融資需求。

## 財政借款與準備金管理凸顯供給背景

美國財政部公布的6月預算數據，為殖利率上升增添了盤末的財政面因素。聯邦政府當月錄得$1,203億赤字，2025年6月則為$270億盈餘。收入較一年前下降5.8%至$4,958億，支出增加23.4%至$6,161億。

截至6月的會計年度赤字，從去年同期的$1.337兆擴大2.2%至$1.367兆。淨利息支出達$8,272億，財政部債券的利息支出總額為$1.052兆。6月向公眾借款$1,661億，本會計年度迄今則為$1.340兆。

數據於美東時間14:00公布，只可能影響週一後半段交易，無法解釋稍早由油價與Waller談話驅動的重新定價。不過，這份報告仍強化了長天期債券長期面臨的供給問題：即使當前較高的借款成本尚未完全傳導至整體債務存量，利息支出已占用聯邦政府大量資源。

短期供給未見明顯需求不足。財政部標售$920億的91天期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.760%，投標倍數2.84倍。間接投標者取得獲接受競爭性投標的56.76%，直接投標者占8.24%，一級交易商獲配34.99%。這批國庫券於7月16日交割，10月15日到期。

規模$790.01億的182天期國庫券標售，投標覆蓋更強，間接投標者占比也更高。最高得標利率為3.860%，投標倍數3.11倍；間接投標者取得66.49%，直接投標者占8.09%，交易商占25.42%。這批券同樣於7月16日交割，並在2027年1月14日到期。由於缺乏標售前的比較基準，結果只能確認現金投資人參與踴躍及投標者組成，無法判斷成交水準相對當時市場交易是偏貴或偏便宜。

聯準會另將截至8月13日之月度期間的準備金管理購債規模維持在約$100億，與前兩個週期相同。紐約聯準銀行交易台在此期間也計畫進行約$176億的再投資購債。

購債規模維持不變，是在當前融資環境寬鬆與年底前預期資金流失之間取得平衡。財政部預計將現金餘額重建至逾$1兆，同時增加國庫券供給，這兩項行動都會從銀行體系抽走流動性。因此，即使聯準會已把每月購債速度從12月的$400億降至4月的$250億、5月的$100億，仍持續透過買進剩餘期限不到一年的美國公債增加準備金。

目前條件使聯準會無須再次提高購債規模。7月8日銀行準備金為$3.14兆，高於2025年底的$2.85兆。相較於擔保品，現金供給一直相當充裕；過去一個月大部分時間，擔保隔夜融資利率都定在準備金餘額利率之下，近期更降至約六週最低。

這些條件凸顯當日短端市場的兩種信號。2年期公債因預期政策路徑轉趨鷹派而遭到拋售，國庫券與擔保融資市場卻持續反映現金充裕。聯準會的準備金購債處理的是政策操作與流動性，而非貨幣政策立場；維持購債規模不變，並未削弱Waller在核心通膨居高不下時提高政策利率的意願。

## 全球長天期債券面臨能源、通膨與政策反轉

日本政府據報無意調整政府年金投資基金的策略性資產配置，使7月10日曾支撐日本公債的潛在退休基金買盤題材明確反轉。消息公布後，日圓一度貶值0.4%至1美元兌162.36日圓，日本公債則擴大跌幅。

日本財務大臣片山皋月呼籲大型公共退休基金增加國內投資後，市場對配置轉變的揣測升溫。GPIF管理約$1.8兆資產，國內債券、國內股票、外國債券及外國股票各占四分之一；即使只是逐步調整，也可能影響日圓與較長天期日本公債的需求。

最新消息排除了立即進行策略性重分配的可能性，但未完全消除漸進調整的空間。政府仍可鼓勵基金在現有允許範圍內運作；內閣官房長官木原稔也表示，GPIF會定期檢視持倉，並可在適當時機調整。市場參與者因此仍可能關注日常再平衡及偏離區間的運用。

正式調整策略須經GPIF的審查程序，並提出符合其對退休金受益人責任的投資理由。該基金在2025年3月維持四類資產各占25%的配置，並把目標周邊允許的偏離幅度從6至8個百分點縮小至5至6個百分點。過去十年大部分時間，外國股票與債券的表現也優於日本資產，因此若只依據預期報酬，提高國內資產配置較難獲得合理支持。

這項反轉使日本長天期債券原有壓力依然存在。市場對首相高市早苗支出計畫的財政疑慮、日圓疲弱，以及對日本央行政策正常化速度過慢的擔憂，持續壓抑較長天期債券。下一次20年期公債標售將在不再假設大型退休基金即將策略轉向的情況下，直接檢驗市場需求。

經濟學家把中東衝突再起納入預測後，歐元區展望也惡化。7月3日至8日受訪的56名經濟學家，對2026年經濟成長率的預測中位數為0.5%，低於一個月前的0.7%，也不及歐洲央行0.8%的基準預測。衝突與荷莫茲海峽運輸受阻，削弱能源運輸恢復的信心；歐洲央行管理委員會委員Yannis Stournaras因此表示，戰事再起讓央行回到先前面臨的難題。

經濟學家對2026年通膨率的預測中位數為2.8%。由於油價先前下跌，這項數字略低於上月預測，但部分跌幅其後已經逆轉，且通膨仍遠高於歐洲央行2%的目標。受訪者預期繼6月升息後，9月會再升息1碼，首次降息則要到2027年9月。歐元區的總體環境因而對債券更加不利：成長預測轉弱，仍未取代央行因通膨高於目標而採取行動的預期。

印度在紐約收盤前公布已實現的通膨加速。綜合消費者物價通膨率從5月的3.93%升至6月的4.38%，食品通膨率由4.78%升至5.32%。農村通膨達4.74%，高於城市地區的3.92%。綜合CPI指數從105.91升至107.00，食品指數則從105.35升至107.15。

通膨的廣度與組成，為市場研判印度央行政策及印度政府公債提供了更偏緊縮的依據。食品仍是重要推力，城市以外地區的通膨也更強。這份數據沒有可獨立核實的同期調查預測作為比較，但相較5月的加速相當明確。

其他新興市場央行也在政策週期的不同階段面臨類似的能源與通膨壓力。衣索比亞央行把政策利率從15%提高至16%，是這項基準利率兩年前推出以來首次升息。央行同時取消商業銀行放款年增率24%的上限，但仍強調政策必須維持緊縮，才能在中期把通膨降至個位數。

衣索比亞5月通膨率為13.4%；伊朗衝突推高燃料與肥料成本後，通膨已回升至10%以上。央行預期通膨會在12月前放緩，但未來六個月仍將維持兩位數。取消信用成長上限、同時提高政策利率，是把政策控制方式從直接的數量限制轉向價格工具，但抗通膨目標並未放寬。

在奈及利亞，渣打銀行把2026年平均通膨率預測從12%調高至15.5%，並預期寬鬆週期將放慢。該行目前預估今年共降息150個基點，使政策利率於年底降至25%。奈及利亞央行2月降息50個基點後，5月把利率維持在26.5%。

奈及利亞央行6月調查顯示，通膨感受指數從44.8微升至45；受訪者把能源成本、治安不穩、借款成本與匯率列為主要壓力。渣打預期7月15日公布的6月通膨率將從15.9%升至16%以上，但調查受訪者預期7月及其後六個月會略為放緩。

印尼則獲得較正面的信用訊號。標普全球評級確認印尼BBB主權評級與穩定展望，與穆迪和惠譽今年稍早給予的負面展望形成對比。標普援引印尼過往的財政紀律，並預期GDP 3%的法定赤字上限將繼續作為政策錨點。

這項決定在6月債券遭到拋售後，消除了眼前的降評疑慮，但未排除治理、財政執行與資本流動方面的問題。標普預期政府會把免費供餐計畫的支出，較原定$166億預算削減約三分之一，並認為資源產業更集中的管控有助於增加收入。消息公布後，印尼10年期美元債收復部分稍早跌幅，但仍下跌0.4美分至100.9美分；本幣債券跌幅收窄，印尼盾市場則已收盤。

## 信用市場拓展融資結構

美債殖利率上升、風險情緒轉弱，使上市債務工具承壓，但價格走勢尚未顯示信用利差全面失序。投資級債券基金LQD下跌0.47%，高收益債基金HYG與JNK分別下跌0.24%和0.18%，新興市場債基金EMB則下跌0.64%。

信用市場更關鍵的發展，是人工智慧基礎設施的融資需求日益超出一般無擔保公司債所能負荷。超大規模雲端業者迄今高度依賴投資級市場，利用龐大的資產負債表與現金流，以相對窄的利差籌措數十億美元。摩根大通分析師表示，部分投資人正接近單一發行人限額；巴克萊則認為，僅靠無擔保債券已不足以支應計畫中的資本形成規模。

資料中心債券正成為替代方案之一。這類證券把科技租戶支付的租金現金流組合起來，投資人取得的並非對營運公司的單純直接債權。其信用品質取決於租戶的付款能力、租約保障強度、工程能否完工、電力供應、正常運作時間，以及設施達到穩定營運前仍由專案承擔的剩餘風險。

這種結構同時改變信用分析與定價。習慣承作Amazon或Microsoft資產負債表風險的投資人，必須改為評估長期合約、開發商、實體基礎設施與專案施工進度。額外的複雜性可能要求比傳統超大規模業者債券更高的補償，從而提高資本成本，也可能使部署速度更加不均。

隨著融資需求增加，信用保護需求也在擴大。加拿大皇家銀行1月開始為美元單一名稱信用違約交換造市，並計畫隨著更完整的衍生性商品業務成形，增添歐元計價合約。該行表示，6月單一名稱CDS交易量接近今年迄今平均水準的4倍，信用指數選擇權交易量則較一年前倍增。

RBC把這項擴張歸因於大型科技公司創紀錄的發債規模，以及投資人與交易商對集中曝險的避險需求。市場復甦也促使銀行在企業發債時推出新的交換合約，並擴大信用、股票與利率之間的相對價值交易。市場成長本身不代表企業信用品質惡化，但顯示AI借款的規模與集中度正在提高風險移轉需求。

Robinhood則尋求不同的定期融資來源。該公司正在試探市場對至少$4億資產擔保證券的需求，擔保資產是其品牌信用卡的應收帳款，發行規模可能增至$5億。最高評級券次的初步定價指引，約為較基準利率高80個基點。交易由富國銀行與巴克萊安排。

這可能是Robinhood首筆同類交易，也正值公司把業務從證券經紀擴展至消費信用卡。其信用卡帳戶由Coastal Community Bank持有。今年以來，信用卡發行人已透過資產擔保市場籌得逾$110億，包括Capital One前一週規模$38.5億的交易。

高盛另提出一項結構，讓大型私募市場投資人買進提供給其所投資基金的資本承諾融資。這類認購融資可銜接基金完成收購與其後向投資人調用已承諾資本之間的期間。穆迪估計，這個市場規模已增至$1.3兆。

依高盛提案，獨立管理帳戶中的投資人可賺取已動用融資的利息，目前約為較基準利率高160至210個基點；銀行則能釋出資產負債表容量，並保留部分額外利差。這種結構不會實質改變基金經理人取得資本承諾融資額度的能力，但會把更多融資曝險移轉給最終提供承諾股本的投資人。

主權借款人也利用有利的需求環境管理再融資壓力。肯亞正考慮在截至2027年6月的會計年度買回最多$5億國際債券，並發行新的美元債為買回提供資金。實際金額將取決於投資人需求，任何超額募集資金都可能用於支應預算，目前尚未作成最終決定。

若交易落實，這將是肯亞兩年內第四次買回債券。該國外債總額為$437億，其中欠國際債券投資人$106億；國際貨幣基金把肯亞列為債務困境高風險國家。肯亞2月透過雙券次債券籌得$22.5億，此前也曾利用國際發債為到期債務再融資並支應預算。

智利面臨的即時困境較小，但潛在發債計畫更大。其美元主權債利差自3月底以來收窄24個基點，至較美債高82個基點，接近2007年以來最窄水準。參議院批准2026年額外借款$62億，財政部並計畫在今年剩餘期間於國際市場發行$52億債券，計價貨幣可能不只美元與歐元。

有利的市場窗口與轉弱的財政及經濟基本面形成對比。智利已放棄在2030年前平衡結構性預算的目標，現改以相當於GDP 1.5%的赤字為目標。經濟活動已連續五個月較一年前萎縮，減稅預計會降低收入，未償債務也接近部分投資人認為可能引發降評風險的GDP 45%區間。智利幾乎所有能源都仰賴進口，油價也是另一項限制。

美國地方公共融資將帶來另一項需求考驗。Aquarion Water Authority計畫於7月14日發行$24億債券，為收購Eversource Energy旗下自來水公用事業籌資，這將是康乃狄克州史上規模最大的市政債交易。標普給予其中$18.3億優先債券A-評級，另有$5.472億次順位債務獲評BBB+。

債務償付與基礎設施支出將需要大幅調高客戶費率。Aquarion預估明年費率將提高略逾8%，之後至2035年每年漲幅都超過6%。該機構計畫於2026至2036年間投資$24億，包括更換管線、現代化處理廠，以及遵守聯邦政府對持久性化學物質的規定。Aquarion主張，免稅融資、不必支付股東報酬及公司所得稅，可在最初十年為客戶節省$3.66億；但這條費率路徑仍引發反對。

英鎊信用市場對規模較小的投機級借款人也仍然開放。製作多數James Bond電影的Pinewood Group，在可能發行固定利率英鎊債券前開始與投資人會面。該公司獲標普評為BB-、惠譽評為BBB-；上次發行的是2030年到期、票息6%的£7.5億債券，另有一筆£3億債券將於2027年11月到期。新債是否發行仍視市場狀況而定。

## 未來市場意涵

7月14日美東時間08:30公布的美國6月CPI與實質薪資，是檢驗Waller有條件緊縮信號及短端拋售的第一項關鍵數據。整體通膨率預計將受先前汽油價格下跌壓低，但政策判斷會更取決於核心通膨、服務、商品及每月價格上漲的廣度。Waller已區分連續數次較低讀數與單一有利數據；核心通膨若再度強勁，近期採取行動的理由將更為迫切。

Warsh將於美東時間10:00在眾議院金融服務委員會進行就任聯準會主席後首次國會聽證。他對通膨組成的解讀，將決定市場把Waller的警告視為個人設定的門檻，還是整個委員會立場廣泛轉變的一環。參議院聽證會將於7月15日10:00舉行，此前08:30將公布PPI與紐約州製造業調查。

能源仍是連結這些數據與週一市場走勢的關鍵條件。美國定於7月14日美東時間16:00恢復封鎖伊朗船運；EIA則將於7月15日10:30公布截至7月10日當週的石油報告，更新原油、成品油與煉油廠供需狀況。荷莫茲海峽若持續受阻，或汽油與餾分油供應進一步承壓，7月能源成本便會朝與6月CPI參考期間相反的方向發展。

亞洲時段首先公布中國6月與上半年貿易數據，日本則將標售約¥7,000億的20年期公債。日本標售結果預計於7月14日日本時間12:35左右公布；在GPIF立即調整配置的可能性下降後，這是對超長天期債券需求最直接的考驗。中國出口、進口與貿易餘額則將更新區域成長及大宗商品需求前景。

印度6月批發物價與生產者物價數據隨後於7月14日印度時間12:00公布，可觀察消費者與食品通膨上升是否也受到能源及投入成本強化。歐元區7月15日公布的工業生產，則會針對新近下修至0.5%的經濟成長預測，提供已實現的活動數據檢驗。

美國財政部將於7月14日美東時間11:30標售$950億的42天期國庫券，在週一3個月及6個月期標售投標踴躍後，繼續檢驗現金需求。聯準會7月15日14:00公布的褐皮書，接著將提供各地區需求、就業，以及企業轉嫁較高成本能力的證據。

下一項更廣泛的美國成長檢驗在7月16日到來：零售銷售、初領失業救濟金人數與費城聯準銀行調查將於美東時間08:30公布，庫存與銷售數據於10:00公布，聯準會每週資產負債表則於16:30發布。這些資料有助於判斷實質殖利率上升，是否除了通膨外也受到需求韌性支撐。

近期最核心的問題，是週一行情究竟只是一場短暫的地緣政治衝擊，還是聯準會政策路徑的持久轉變。船運恢復、核心通膨放緩，加上Warsh傾向耐心觀望的評估，將減輕集中於短端的壓力。反之，若荷莫茲海峽持續受阻或通膨再度廣泛上升，聯準會便會面對Waller所指出的組合：經濟具有韌性、基礎物價上升，加上距離7月會議甚近的新一波能源衝擊，使進一步緊縮仍是必須實際考量的決策。

overall_summary.headline: 油價飆升、Waller使7月升息成為可能，美債遭拋售並呈空頭趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國與伊朗再度爆發衝突，推動油價急升；聯準會理事Christopher Waller又表示，是否近期再次升息取決於下一份核心通膨數據，美債因而遭到拋售，殖利率曲線呈空頭趨平。2年期殖利率上升7.6個基點至4.285%，10年期上升6.3個基點至4.625%，30年期增加4.5個基點至5.106%。2年與10年期利差收窄1.3個基點至34個基點；貨幣市場則把7月升息的隱含機率，從盤中稍早不到40%提高至約50%。

新一輪攻擊發生，加上Trump宣布7月14日恢復封鎖伊朗船隻，WTI上漲9.42%至$78.14，布蘭特原油上漲9.59%至$83.30。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步上升，顯示投資人同時反映更大的通膨衝擊與聯準會更緊縮的回應。

科技股領跌與波動率上升強化了市場的防禦氣氛，卻未帶來美債買盤。殖利率上升占據主導，美元走強、黃金下跌。國庫券標售需求強勁、準備金充裕且擔保融資環境寬鬆，顯示並未發生全面性融資失序；6月聯邦赤字凸顯的是長期借款負擔，而非早盤拋售的原因。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off on July 13 as renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities pushed oil sharply higher and Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller made another near-term rate increase explicitly conditional on the next core-inflation reading. The 2-year yield rose 7.6 basis points to 4.285%, its highest area since February 2025, while the 5-year climbed 7.1 basis points to 4.377%, the 10-year increased 6.3 basis points to 4.625%, and the 30-year added 4.5 basis points to 5.106%.

The concentration of losses at shorter maturities produced a bear flattening. The 2s10s curve narrowed 1.3 basis points to 34 basis points, and 2s30s compressed 3.1 basis points to 82.1 basis points. Money markets raised the implied probability of a July increase to roughly 50% from less than 40% earlier in the session after Waller said another hot core reading would require the Federal Open Market Committee to consider tightening in the near term.

That policy repricing came as the energy shock regained force. WTI jumped 9.42% to $78.14 and Brent rose 9.59% to $83.30 after the United States and Iran exchanged fresh strikes and President Donald Trump announced the reinstatement of a blockade on Iranian ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. He also demanded a 20% reimbursement on other cargo using the waterway. Observable crossings had already slowed sharply, and the latest escalation undermined expectations that traffic and oil inventories would normalize soon.

Both real rates and inflation compensation contributed to the Treasury move. The 10-year real yield rose 3.6 basis points to 2.336%, while the 10-year breakeven increased 2.7 basis points to 2.289%. The combination showed investors pricing a larger current inflation impulse while also demanding a higher inflation-adjusted return as the Fed’s reaction function became more restrictive. The move was not simply a long-run fear that energy would lift prices: the front end led because Waller connected broad core inflation directly to the possibility of action at an approaching meeting.

Risk assets reinforced the defensive character of the session without generating demand for government bonds. The S&P 500 fell 0.79%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.88%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.78% as a severe Korean technology selloff spread into U.S. trading. The dollar index gained 0.31%, while gold futures fell 2.61% to $3,997 as higher yields and a firmer dollar outweighed geopolitical demand. The VIX rose 14.17% to 17.16.

The day nevertheless stopped short of a generalized funding disruption. Treasury’s 3- and 6-month bill auctions attracted substantial bids, secured funding had remained soft, and the Fed kept its monthly reserve-management purchases at $10 billion. The distinction was important: the market imposed a higher policy and inflation premium across the coupon curve, but cash investors continued to absorb short government paper as the financial system carried ample reserves.

## Oil and Waller Pull Tightening Risk Toward July

The immediate catalyst was a renewed deterioration around the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. forces conducted further strikes after an attack on a container ship, while Iran retaliated against U.S. allies and bases in the region. Washington and Tehran issued conflicting statements about whether the strait was open, but observable crossings had nearly ceased and total transits fell to their lowest level in a month on Sunday.

Trump then said the United States was reinstating its blockade of Iranian ships and would seek a 20% reimbursement on all other cargo moving through Hormuz. Tehran accepted the principle that whoever provided safe passage could receive compensation but called the proposed rate excessive. The White House did not explain how the charge would be administered or whether Gulf allies had agreed to it.

The scale of the proposed charge would be commercially significant if implemented. At prevailing oil prices, a 20% payment on a fully loaded very large crude carrier would amount to about $32 million, compared with Iranian tolls previously described as reaching roughly $2 million. U.S. Central Command said the renewed blockade would begin July 14 at 16:00 ET, making it an announced future condition rather than part of Monday’s physical shipping regime. The announcement itself affected Monday’s assessment because it reduced the prospect of an early normalization in traffic.

Oil’s response was correspondingly large. Brent gained more than 9% at the New York close after trading through $80 during the session, while WTI posted its biggest daily increase in more than 3 months. Even after that advance, both benchmarks remained below earlier wartime peaks, but the direction reversed the immediate energy relief that had accompanied the July 10 Treasury session. The bond market therefore had to price both the renewed supply risk and the possibility that another fuel increase would reinforce already elevated underlying inflation.

Waller made that second channel explicit. The Fed governor said policymakers would need to consider tightening in the near term if this week’s data delivered another hot reading on core inflation. He described the economy as being in good shape, with stable labor conditions and resilient consumer demand, but said policy had reached a crossroads because tariffs, energy prices and artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending were adding to price pressure.

His concern was not limited to the renewed rise in crude. Core personal consumption expenditures inflation reached 3.4% in the year through May and had been increasing since January, before the latest U.S.-Iran war began. Waller argued that the rise in underlying inflation had become sufficiently persistent to require attention to its breadth, rather than being dismissed as a temporary energy disturbance.

The qualification was equally important. Waller said several months of lower core readings would be needed to establish that inflation was moving in the right direction, but he continued to regard such an outcome as plausible. If it occurred, he would support holding rates steady. He also noted that the labor market was not displaying the excess tightness seen during the 2021–22 inflation episode and that inflation expectations remained anchored.

That left his preference conditional rather than an unconditional call for an immediate increase. A cooler core reading would preserve the hold; another strong result would move the near-term tightening case forward. The Fed held its target rate unanimously at the June meeting, although the minutes showed that a few officials had seen a case for an increase. Half of the 18 policymakers submitting forecasts expected at least one quarter-point increase during 2026, while Chair Kevin Warsh did not submit a rate projection.

Treasury pricing responded most strongly where that conditionality matters. The 2-year yield rose slightly more than the 5- and 10-year yields and substantially more than the 30-year. The 2s30s curve has now flattened 6.5 basis points over a month even though all four benchmark yields are higher over that period. Investors have increased compensation for both inflation and restrictive policy, but the latest increment was concentrated around the path of upcoming FOMC decisions.

The 10-year decomposition showed that neither component alone explained the selloff. The 2.7-basis-point increase in breakevens reflected a renewed inflation premium as oil surged. The 3.6-basis-point rise in the real yield captured the accompanying expectation that the Fed would respond, as well as the continuing burden from resilient activity and heavy public and private borrowing. The nominal 10-year yield rose to its highest level since May.

Trading activity expanded with the move. Treasury cash-market par activity reached $924.2 billion, 15% more than in the previous session, while nominal-coupon activity rose 16.4% to $721.8 billion. Turnover in maturities longer than 7 years and no more than 10 years increased 32.2% to $126.5 billion. Those figures measure two-way transactions rather than investor direction, but they place the selloff in a more active session, particularly around the benchmark sector.

The cross-asset reaction also reflected more than the energy shock. South Korea’s technology market suffered another violent reversal after a year of extraordinary gains. The MSCI Korea Index had risen more than 250% in the 12 months through June, but was 28% below its June high after Monday’s decline. SK Hynix fell a record 15% in Seoul, and its U.S. depositary shares lost 9.3% as concerns about crowded artificial-intelligence exposures reached American trading.

That decline contrasted with TSMC’s 36% increase in quarterly sales to NT$1.27 trillion, including a 68% year-on-year rise in June. The divergence did not show that artificial-intelligence demand had collapsed; it showed that strong operating results could coexist with unusually fragile positioning and valuation. For rates, that matters because the AI buildout remains both a source of real demand and a source of very large financing requirements even as related equities become more volatile.

## Fiscal Borrowing and Reserve Management Keep the Supply Backdrop in View

The Treasury’s June budget statement added a late-session fiscal dimension to the rise in yields. The federal government recorded a $120.3 billion deficit for the month, compared with a $27 billion surplus in June 2025. Receipts fell 5.8% from a year earlier to $495.8 billion, while outlays rose 23.4% to $616.1 billion.

For the fiscal year through June, the deficit widened 2.2% to $1.367 trillion from $1.337 trillion in the comparable period. Net interest reached $827.2 billion, and gross interest on Treasury debt securities totaled $1.052 trillion. Borrowing from the public was $166.1 billion during June and $1.340 trillion for the fiscal year to date.

Released at 14:00 ET, the statement could inform only the latter portion of Monday trading and does not explain the earlier oil- and Waller-driven repricing. It nevertheless reinforced the longer-running supply problem confronting duration: interest expense is already absorbing a large share of federal resources even before higher current borrowing costs pass fully through the debt stock.

Short-term supply encountered no obvious demand shortfall. Treasury’s $92.000 billion 91-day bill auction stopped at a 3.760% high rate with a 2.84 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received 56.76% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders took 8.24%, and primary dealers were allotted 34.99%. The bills settle July 16 and mature October 15.

The $79.001 billion 182-day auction produced stronger cover and a larger indirect share. It stopped at 3.860% with a 3.11 bid-to-cover ratio; indirect bidders received 66.49%, direct bidders 8.09%, and dealers 25.42%. Those securities also settle July 16 and mature January 14, 2027. Without pre-auction references, the results establish substantial cash participation and the bidder mix, but not whether either sale cleared rich or cheap to prevailing trading.

The Federal Reserve separately maintained its reserve-management purchases at about $10 billion for the monthly period ending August 13, unchanged from the previous 2 cycles. The New York Fed’s trading desk also plans about $17.6 billion of reinvestment purchases over the period.

The steady purchase amount balances comfortable current funding conditions against an expected drain later in the year. Treasury is projected to rebuild its cash balance to more than $1 trillion while increasing bill supply, moves that withdraw liquidity from the banking system. The Fed has therefore continued adding reserves through purchases of Treasuries with less than a year remaining, even after reducing the monthly pace from $40 billion in December to $25 billion in April and $10 billion in May.

Current conditions allowed the Fed to avoid another increase. Bank reserves stood at $3.14 trillion on July 8, up from $2.85 trillion at the end of 2025. Cash had been abundant relative to collateral, and the Secured Overnight Financing Rate had fixed below the interest rate on reserve balances for most of the previous month, recently reaching its lowest level in roughly 6 weeks.

That combination separates the day’s two front-end signals. The 2-year note sold off because the expected policy path became more hawkish, while Treasury bills and secured funding continued to reflect ample cash. The Fed’s reserve purchases address implementation and liquidity, not the stance of monetary policy; keeping them unchanged did not dilute Waller’s willingness to tighten the policy rate if core inflation remained high.

## Global Duration Faces Energy, Inflation and Policy Reversals

Japan supplied a clear reversal of the prospective pension-demand story that had supported government bonds on July 10. The yen weakened as much as 0.4% to 162.36 per dollar and JGBs extended losses after a report that the government had no plans to overhaul the Government Pension Investment Fund’s strategic asset allocation.

Speculation about a shift had intensified after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama urged large public pension funds to increase domestic investment. Because GPIF oversees about $1.8 trillion and allocates one-quarter each to domestic bonds, domestic equities, foreign bonds and foreign equities, even a gradual change could affect the yen and demand for longer JGBs.

The latest account removed the prospect of an immediate strategic reallocation without eliminating all scope for incremental change. The government could encourage funds to work within existing permitted ranges, and Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said GPIF routinely reviews its holdings and can make amendments when appropriate. Market participants may therefore continue watching day-to-day rebalancing and the use of deviation bands.

A formal strategic change would require GPIF’s review process and an investment justification consistent with its duty to pension beneficiaries. The fund retained its equal 25% allocations in March 2025 and narrowed the permitted deviation around those targets to 5–6 percentage points from 6–8 percentage points. Foreign stocks and bonds have also outperformed Japanese assets over much of the past decade, making a larger domestic allocation harder to justify solely on expected returns.

The reversal leaves Japan’s underlying duration pressures in place. Fiscal concern surrounding Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s spending plans, a weak yen and anxiety that the Bank of Japan is normalizing too slowly have continued to weigh on longer maturities. The next 20-year auction will therefore test demand without the assumption that a large strategic pension shift is imminent.

The euro-area outlook also deteriorated as economists incorporated the renewed Middle East conflict. The median forecast of 56 economists surveyed July 3–8 put 2026 growth at 0.5%, down from 0.7% a month earlier and below the European Central Bank’s 0.8% baseline. Hostilities and disrupted Hormuz traffic reduced confidence that energy shipments would recover, prompting ECB Governing Council member Yannis Stournaras to say the renewed fighting had taken the central bank back to its earlier problem.

Economists’ median inflation projection for 2026 was 2.8%, slightly below the previous month’s forecast after an earlier fall in oil that has since partly reversed, but still well above the ECB’s 2% target. Respondents expected another quarter-point rate increase in September, following the June hike, and did not anticipate the first reduction until September 2027. The euro-area mix is therefore becoming less favorable for bonds: weaker projected growth has not yet displaced the expected response to above-target inflation.

India reported a realized inflation acceleration before the New York close. Combined consumer-price inflation rose to 4.38% in June from 3.93% in May, while food inflation increased to 5.32% from 4.78%. Rural inflation reached 4.74%, compared with 3.92% in urban areas. The combined CPI index increased to 107.00 from 105.91, and the food index rose to 107.15 from 105.35.

The breadth and composition add a firmer input for Reserve Bank of India expectations and Indian government bonds. Food remained a significant contributor, and inflation was stronger outside urban centers. The release did not come with an independent contemporaneous survey comparison, but the acceleration from May was clear.

Other emerging-market central banks confronted similar energy and inflation pressure at different stages of their policy cycles. Ethiopia’s central bank raised its policy rate to 16% from 15%, the first increase since the benchmark was introduced 2 years earlier. It simultaneously removed a 24% ceiling on annual commercial-bank credit growth while maintaining that policy needed to remain tight to return inflation to single digits over the medium term.

Ethiopian inflation was 13.4% in May and had climbed back above 10% after the Iran conflict raised fuel and fertilizer costs. The central bank expects inflation to moderate by December but remain in double digits over the next 6 months. Removing the credit cap while raising the policy rate shifts control from a direct quantitative restriction toward a price-based instrument, but does not represent an easing of the inflation objective.

In Nigeria, Standard Chartered raised its forecast for average 2026 inflation to 15.5% from 12% and projected a slower easing cycle. The bank now expects 150 basis points of cuts this year, taking the policy rate to 25% by year-end. The Central Bank of Nigeria held at 26.5% in May after reducing the rate by 50 basis points in February.

The bank’s June survey showed the inflation-perception index edging up to 45 from 44.8, with respondents identifying energy costs, insecurity, borrowing costs and the exchange rate as the leading pressures. Standard Chartered expects June inflation, due July 15, to exceed 16% after 15.9%, although survey respondents anticipated some moderation in July and over the following 6 months.

Indonesia received a more supportive credit signal. S&P Global Ratings affirmed its BBB sovereign rating and stable outlook, contrasting with the negative outlooks assigned earlier in the year by Moody’s Ratings and Fitch Ratings. S&P cited the country’s history of fiscal discipline and expected the statutory deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP to remain a policy anchor.

The decision removed an immediate downgrade concern after a June bond selloff, though it did not erase questions about governance, fiscal execution or capital flows. S&P expects the government to reduce spending on its free-meals program by about one-third from the original $16.6 billion budget and sees greater centralized control of the resources sector supporting revenue. Indonesia’s 10-year dollar bond erased part of an earlier decline after the announcement but remained 0.4 cent lower at 100.9 cents; local bonds pared losses, while the rupiah market had already closed.

## Credit Markets Broaden Their Funding Structures

Higher Treasury yields and weaker risk sentiment pressured listed debt instruments, though the price moves did not establish a broad spread dislocation. The LQD investment-grade fund fell 0.47%, high-yield funds HYG and JNK lost 0.24% and 0.18%, respectively, and the EMB emerging-market debt fund declined 0.64%.

The more consequential credit development was the growing need to finance artificial-intelligence infrastructure outside ordinary unsecured corporate bonds. Hyperscalers have so far relied heavily on the investment-grade market, using their large balance sheets and cash flows to raise billions of dollars at relatively narrow spreads. Analysts at JPMorgan said some investors are approaching single-issuer limits, while Barclays argued that unsecured bonds alone are becoming insufficient for the scale of planned capital formation.

Data-center bonds are emerging as one alternative. These securities bundle lease payments from technology tenants rather than giving investors a simple direct claim on the operating company. Their credit quality depends on the tenant’s ability to pay, the strength of lease protections, construction completion, access to power, uptime and the residual project risk before the facility is stabilized.

That structure changes both analysis and pricing. Investors accustomed to underwriting an Amazon or Microsoft balance sheet must instead assess long-term contracts, developers, physical infrastructure and project execution. The additional complexity is likely to require more compensation than conventional hyperscaler debt, raising the cost of capital and potentially making the pace of deployment less uniform.

Demand for protection is expanding alongside those financing needs. Royal Bank of Canada began making markets in U.S. dollar single-name credit-default swaps in January and plans to add euro-denominated contracts as it develops a fuller derivatives franchise. The bank said its June single-name CDS trading volume was almost 4 times its year-to-date pace, while credit-index-options volume had doubled from a year earlier.

RBC linked the expansion to record Big Tech issuance and the need for investors and dealers to hedge concentrated exposure. The resurgence is also encouraging banks to launch new swaps when companies issue bonds and to expand relative-value activity between credit, equities and rates. The growth of the market does not itself establish worsening corporate quality, but it shows that the scale and concentration of AI borrowing are creating greater demand for risk transfer.

Robinhood is pursuing a different source of term funding. The company is gauging demand for at least $400 million of asset-backed securities supported by receivables from its branded credit cards, potentially increasing the sale to $500 million. Initial guidance for the highest-rated tranche was about 80 basis points over its benchmark. Wells Fargo and Barclays are arranging the transaction.

The prospective deal would be Robinhood’s first of its kind and comes as the company expands beyond brokerage into consumer cards. Its card accounts are owned by Coastal Community Bank. Credit-card issuers have raised more than $11 billion in the asset-backed market this year, including Capital One’s $3.85 billion transaction the previous week.

Goldman Sachs is separately proposing a structure that would allow large private-market investors to buy capital-call loans extended to their own funds. Those subscription facilities bridge the period between a fund’s acquisition and the eventual drawdown of committed investor capital. Moody’s estimates the market has grown to $1.3 trillion.

Under Goldman’s proposal, investors in separately managed accounts could earn the interest on drawn facilities, currently about 160–210 basis points over the benchmark, while the bank releases balance-sheet capacity and retains part of the additional spread. The structure would not materially change the fund manager’s access to a capital-call line, but it would transfer more of the financing exposure to the investors that ultimately provide the committed equity.

Sovereign borrowers are also using favorable demand to manage refinancing pressure. Kenya is considering buying back as much as $500 million of Eurobonds during the fiscal year ending June 2027 and issuing new dollar debt to fund the repurchase. The amount would depend on investor appetite, and any excess proceeds could finance the budget. No final decision has been made.

A transaction would be Kenya’s fourth buyback in 2 years. The country has $43.7 billion of external debt, including $10.6 billion owed to Eurobond investors, and the International Monetary Fund classifies it as being at high risk of debt distress. Kenya raised $2.25 billion through dual-tranche notes in February after using earlier international sales to refinance maturities and support the budget.

Chile faces less immediate distress but a larger prospective issuance program. Its sovereign dollar spread had tightened 24 basis points since the end of March to 82 basis points over Treasuries, close to its narrowest level since 2007. The Senate authorized an additional $6.2 billion of borrowing for 2026, and the Finance Ministry plans to sell $5.2 billion internationally over the remainder of the year, potentially in currencies beyond dollars and euros.

The favorable market window contrasts with weakening fiscal and economic fundamentals. Chile abandoned its goal of balancing the structural budget by 2030 and now targets a deficit of 1.5% of GDP. Economic activity has contracted from a year earlier for 5 consecutive months, tax cuts are expected to reduce revenue, and outstanding debt is approaching the 45%-of-GDP area that some investors associate with downgrade risk. Oil is another constraint because Chile imports almost all of its energy.

Domestic public finance will provide a separate demand test. The Aquarion Water Authority plans to sell $2.4 billion of bonds on July 14, the largest municipal transaction in Connecticut’s history, to finance its purchase of the water utility from Eversource Energy. S&P rated $1.83 billion of senior bonds A- and $547.2 million of subordinate debt BBB+.

Debt service and infrastructure spending will require substantial customer-rate increases. Aquarion projects an increase of a little more than 8% next year, followed by annual rises exceeding 6% through 2035. The authority plans $2.4 billion of investment between 2026 and 2036, including pipe replacement, treatment-plant modernization and compliance with federal rules on persistent chemicals. It argues that tax-exempt financing and the absence of shareholder returns and corporate income tax will save customers $366 million over the first decade, even as the rate path has generated opposition.

Sterling credit also remains accessible to smaller speculative-grade borrowers. Pinewood Group, the studio behind most James Bond films, began investor meetings ahead of a possible fixed-rate sterling offering. The company, rated BB- by S&P and BBB- by Fitch, last issued a £750 million 6% bond due in 2030 and has another £300 million note maturing in November 2027. A new sale remains subject to market conditions.

## Forward Market Significance

June U.S. CPI and real earnings at 08:30 ET on July 14 are the immediate tests of Waller’s conditional tightening signal and the front-end selloff. The headline rate is expected to benefit from an earlier decline in gasoline, but the policy decision will turn more heavily on core inflation, services, goods and the breadth of monthly increases. Waller has already distinguished several cooler readings from a single favorable print; another strong core result would make the case for near-term action more immediate.

Warsh begins his first congressional testimony as Fed chair before the House Financial Services Committee at 10:00 ET. His interpretation of the inflation composition will determine whether markets treat Waller’s warning as an individual threshold or part of a broader Committee shift. The Senate hearing follows at 10:00 on July 15, after PPI and the Empire State manufacturing survey at 08:30.

Energy remains the condition joining those releases to Monday’s market move. The U.S. blockade of Iranian shipping is scheduled to resume at 16:00 ET on July 14, while the EIA petroleum report at 10:30 on July 15 will update crude, product and refinery balances for the week ended July 10. Persistent disruption around Hormuz or further pressure on gasoline and distillate availability would keep July energy costs moving in the opposite direction from the June CPI reference period.

Asia begins with China’s June and first-half trade data and Japan’s approximately ¥700 billion 20-year JGB auction. The Japanese sale, with results expected around 12:35 JST on July 14, is the most direct test of super-long demand after the prospect of an immediate GPIF allocation overhaul receded. China’s exports, imports and trade balance will update the regional growth and commodity-demand picture.

India’s June wholesale and producer-price releases follow at 12:00 IST on July 14. They will show whether the rise in consumer and food inflation is being reinforced by energy and input costs. Euro-area industrial production on July 15 will supply a realized activity check against the newly reduced 0.5% growth forecast.

Treasury’s $95 billion 42-day bill auction at 11:30 ET on July 14 will extend the cash-demand test after the strong coverage of Monday’s 3- and 6-month sales. The Federal Reserve’s Beige Book on July 15 at 14:00 will then add regional evidence on demand, employment and firms’ ability to pass through higher costs.

The next broader U.S. growth test arrives July 16 with retail sales, initial claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey at 08:30 ET, followed by inventories and sales at 10:00 and the Fed’s weekly balance-sheet release at 16:30. Those releases will help determine whether the rise in real yields is being sustained by resilient demand as well as inflation.

The central near-term question is whether Monday marked a temporary geopolitical shock or a durable shift in the policy path. Restored shipping, softer core inflation and a Warsh assessment favoring patience would reduce the pressure concentrated at the front end. Continued Hormuz disruption or another broad inflation increase would leave the Fed facing the combination Waller identified: a resilient economy, rising underlying prices and a fresh energy impulse close enough to the July meeting to make further tightening a live decision.

section_summaries.summary: AI infrastructure financing is expanding beyond ordinary unsecured corporate bonds into data-center structures, while concentrated Big Tech exposure is increasing demand for credit derivatives. Robinhood is exploring credit-card receivable ABS, Goldman is proposing investor-funded capital-call loans, and sovereign and municipal borrowers are testing refinancing and issuance demand under differing fiscal constraints.

The near-term question is whether the selloff marks a temporary geopolitical shock or a durable shift in the Fed path. U.S. inflation data and Warsh’s testimony will test Waller’s conditional warning, while the Hormuz blockade and petroleum balances will show whether the energy impulse persists. Japan’s 20-year auction will separately test super-long demand after expectations of an immediate GPIF reallocation receded.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off and bear-flatten as oil surges and Waller puts a July rate increase in play
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off in a bear flattening as renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities drove oil sharply higher and Fed Governor Christopher Waller made another near-term rate increase conditional on the next core-inflation reading. The 2-year yield rose 7.6 basis points to 4.285%, the 10-year increased 6.3 basis points to 4.625%, and the 30-year added 4.5 basis points to 5.106%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 1.3 basis points to 34 basis points as money markets raised the implied probability of a July increase to roughly 50% from less than 40% earlier in the session.

WTI gained 9.42% to $78.14 and Brent rose 9.59% to $83.30 after fresh strikes and Trump’s announcement that a blockade of Iranian ships would resume on July 14. Both the 10-year real yield and breakeven inflation rose, showing that investors priced a larger inflation impulse alongside a more restrictive Fed response.

Technology-led equity losses and higher volatility reinforced the defensive tone but did not generate Treasury demand. The dollar strengthened and gold fell as higher yields prevailed. Strong bill-auction participation, ample reserves and soft secured funding indicated no generalized funding disruption, while the June federal deficit reinforced the longer-term borrowing burden rather than explaining the initial selloff.
overall_summary.summary: Renewed U.S.-Iran strikes and a planned Hormuz blockade sent oil more than 9% higher, while Waller tied another hot core-inflation reading to near-term tightening, lifting the 2-year yield 7.6 basis points and pulling the curve flatter even as bill demand remained strong and secured funding stayed soft.
